text.p: The Italian debt market closed off highs as operators paused to take profits after another storming session which saw both cash bonds as well as Btp futures post new record highs.

"We saw some profit-taking on the September Btp contract but this only serves to rebuild buying positions," one dealer said who saw the future climbing to 135.50 with a Btp/Bund spread in the 100 basis point area. The spread ended at 94 after a 91 low.
Traders said that there was continuing good support around 136.40, the session's low. September closed 32 bps up at 136.58 after posting a new high at 137.05 but slipped in APT trade.
"When the contract topped 137.00 today cash bonds were left a bit behind and this could be seen as a first sign of profit taking," one trader said adding there were few sellers around.

The benchmark February 2007 Btp gained 29 bps to 102.57 after an afternoon high at 102.91. The March 2002 rose 15 bps to 101.60 after a record 101.80, yielding 5.92 percent. The five year Btp/Bund spread was 155 bps after a midday 154 bps.
The February 2000 Bpt gained five bps to 100.55 to yield 5.83 percent with the spread at 198 bps after an early 196.
On the interbank market, the average overnight rate was 6.99 percent against 6.98 percent at the previous close.
